patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — OpenCart and VTEX share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

OpenCart and VTEX share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose OpenCart only if your buying job matches “GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by” rather than VTEX's shape. Choose VTEX only if your buying job matches “Enterprise commerce SaaS — contact-sales get-started only; no invented floors. Shopify kee” rather than OpenCart's shape. Workflow advantage: OpenCart leans shared coverage; VTEX leans wholesale-b2b. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — OpenCart and VTEX share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: OpenCart is GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by secondary sources (confirm live). WooCommerce kee; VTEX is Enterprise commerce SaaS — contact-sales get-started only; no invented floors. Shopify keeps the SaaS award..
- Company-size focus: OpenCart (small-business, mid-market) vs VTEX (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: OpenCart-leaning — vs VTEX-leaning wholesale-b2b.
- Researched limits: OpenCart — Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0; VTEX — No published self-serve monthly tiles — hard to shortlist on list price alone.

Limitations — OpenCart: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0; Managed cloud floors are not first-party confirmed here — confirm live before budgeting; VTEX: No published self-serve monthly tiles — hard to shortlist on list price alone; Enterprise sales and implementation cycles versus Shopify SMB speed.

Poor-fit cases: OpenCart is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0 · VTEX is a poor fit when that limitation bites: No published self-serve monthly tiles — hard to shortlist on list price alone · Avoid OpenCart if you actually need VTEX's motion (Enterprise commerce SaaS — contact-sales get-started only; no invented floors. S)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
